Job Description
About the Role
Are you passionate about sustainable technology and modern software engineering? Join our cross-functional team in developing the next generation of energy-efficient heating and cooling solutions. In this role, you will help design, implement, and optimize intelligent control and regulation algorithms for state-of-the-art heat pumps, directly contributing to the global energy transition.

Your contribution
Shape the future: Develop control and regulation functions for our latest heat pumps, actively driving forward innovative algorithms for energy-efficient, resource-saving heating and cooling systems.
Take a holistic approach: Guide software functions throughout their full lifecycle—from requirements gathering and concept simulation through to implementation and verification across multiple testing levels (MIL, SIL, HIL).
Realize model-based software: Design and optimize model-based software functions in Matlab/Simulink for the closed-loop control of thermodynamic and hydraulic systems.
Implement software: Apply modern software development practices and text-based languages (e.g., C/C++), utilizing modern engineering and AI-assisted tools to advance embedded software modules.
Validate & test: Commission and test application software on cutting-edge heat pump test benches, supporting rapid prototyping and real-world system validation.
Collaborate cross-functionally: Work in an international, agile environment, collaborating closely with experts across software, electronics, HMI, hydraulics, and thermodynamics.

Qualifications
What You Bring
Education: Degree (Bachelor's or Master's) in Mechatronics, Control Systems, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Process Engineering, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent practical engineering background).
Core Competencies:
Solid foundational understanding of control engineering, mechatronic systems, or thermodynamic processes.
Practical experience in software development—either through model-based development (Matlab/Simulink) or text-based embedded programming (C/C++).
Working familiarity with software testing or simulation concepts (e.g., MIL, SIL, or HIL).
Languages: Working proficiency / business fluency in English (written and spoken).
Mindset: Solution-oriented mindset, strong curiosity for clean energy technologies, and an eagerness to learn and grow within an international team.

Nice to Have
Several years of dedicated industry experience in embedded software or controls engineering.
Knowledge of HVAC systems, refrigeration cycles, or hydraulic systems.
Experience with bus protocols and communication interfaces (e.g., CAN, LIN, Modbus, MQTT).
Familiarity with agile development practices (e.g., Scrum, Kanban) and modern CI/CD tooling (e.g., Git, Jira, Jenkins).

Additional Information
What We Offer
Impactful Mission: Play an active role in decarbonization and sustainable climate technologies.
Flexible Working: Flexible working hours and hybrid work options for an optimal work-life balance.
Continuous Growth: Access to cutting-edge development tools, AI tooling, and tailored technical/language training opportunities.
Collaborative Culture: An open, appreciative, and international team environment with state-of-the-art laboratory and test bench facilities.

Quintus Technologies is looking for a Forwarder to join our logistics team in Västerås.
Here, you will work with international project logistics, coordinating shipments of advanced high-pressure systems to customers around the world. Our equipment often requires carefully planned transport solutions, detailed documentation and close collaboration between several parties.
You will become part of a collaborative logistics team where you have the opportunity to take responsibility, develop your expertise and contribute to successful deliveries worldwide.
About the role
As a Forwarder at Quintus Technologies, you will be responsible for planning and coordinating international shipments, with a particular focus on project logistics and customs-related matters.
You will work closely with project managers, production, purchasing, external freight partners and customs authorities to find suitable transport solutions, ensure compliance with customs regulations and secure efficient, accurate and timely deliveries.
Customs management will be a key focus area of the role, where you will take an active part in developing customs procedures, handling customs-related documentation and staying up to date with international trade regulations.
Your main responsibilities will include:
Requesting, evaluating and comparing transport quotations and selecting suitable freight forwarders.
Preparing and managing shipping documentation, packing lists and product labels.
Handling Letters of Credit (L/C) and ensuring that the required shipping documentation is accurate and complete.
Managing customs documentation, import shipments and relevant import/export requirements.
Maintaining accurate shipping records and updating information in relevant systems.
Coordinating external warehousing and storage solutions when needed.
Taking greater ownership of customs-related matters, proactively developing customs procedures and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations.

Who are you?
We believe you are someone who enjoys working with logistics and takes pride in making sure that everything is handled correctly.
You are structured, thorough and service-minded, with a natural ability to keep track of details and deadlines. You enjoy coordinating different activities, communicating with people and finding solutions when unexpected challenges arise.
You are comfortable taking responsibility for your work and understand the importance of accuracy, particularly when dealing with international shipping documentation and customs requirements.
As a colleague, you are approachable, collaborative and proactive. You enjoy being part of a team while also having the confidence to work independently.
We believe you have:
Education in logistics, freight forwarding or international trade, preferably from a vocational college, or equivalent practical experience.
Knowledge of international transportation, shipping documentation and logistics processes.
Good understanding of customs procedures and import/export requirements.
An interest in international trade, transportation and logistics.
Good communication skills in English and Swedish, both written and spoken.

Experience in freight forwarding, project logistics, Letters of Credit (L/C) or ERP systems is highly valuable.
Most importantly, we are looking for someone with the right mindset, a willingness to learn and the ability to take responsibility for complex logistics activities.
Why join Quintus Technologies?
At Quintus, you will work with logistics that go beyond everyday transportation.
Our advanced high-pressure systems are delivered to customers in industries such as aerospace, automotive, energy and medical technology. Each project brings its own requirements, challenges and opportunities to find smart solutions.
You will join a forwarding team of four people and work closely with colleagues across the organization. Here, collaboration and knowledge-sharing are important, and you will have the opportunity to develop your skills in an international environment.
Quintus combines advanced technology and a global customer base with a welcoming, down-to-earth and family-oriented culture.
If you enjoy variety, responsibility and international collaboration, this could be a great next step in your career.
Location
The position is based in Västerås, Sweden.
About Quintus Technologies
Quintus Technologies specializes in the design, manufacturing, installation and support of high-pressure systems for sheet metal forming, advanced materials densification for high-quality industrial components as well as high pressure processing for food and beverage to deactivate the bacteria.
Headquartered in Västerås, Sweden, and represented in 45 countries worldwide. Quintus is the world leader in high-pressure technology, having delivered more than 1,900 systems globally to customers in industries such as aerospace, automotive, energy and medical implants.
Learn more about us at: www.quintustechnologies.com (http://www.quintustechnologies.com)

Summary: The Pharmacovigilance Specialist for the Nordics is responsible for: in collaboration with the Pharmacovigilance Manager, to maintain an efficient local Pharmacovigilance system in the Nordic countries meeting the European and national regulations and in compliance with the Baxter Pharmacovigilance procedures. To ensure appropriate contacts with the other organizations not limited to country Regulatory Affairs, Country Quality Assurance, Business Units and with HCP and Competent authorities (MPA, FIMEA, DMA, NOMA, IMA). To work closely with the PV team based in UK according to the cluster model.
Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Medicine, or a related field.
3-5 years of experience in Pharmacovigilance, Drug Safety, or a related healthcare/pharmaceutical role.
Fluent in Danish, Swedish, and English, with strong verbal and written communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities in a regulated environment.
Excellent collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a cross-functional team.

Full list of responsibilities
The PV Specialist is accountable and responsible for the following activities:

1. ADR Reporting:
·To collect, document, follow-up all local AEs and other pharmacovigilance information (e.g. pregnancy, medication error, lack of efficacy) from all sources according to SOPs
·To transmit all reports to GPS (Global Patient Safety) in a timely manner
·To make all efforts to answer the queries of the GPS organization and to use the specific follow-up questionnaires
·To answer the safety questions from the Health Care Professionals with the support of the cluster PV Manager, PV Director and the GPS organization, and Medical affairs if necessary
·To close and archive ADR reports according to SOPs

2. Clinical trials activities:
·If stated in the protocol, to process the SAEs and transmit them to the GPS according to SOPs.
3. Audits and inspections
·To act as local PV representative during inspections and audits, actively participating to the inspection/audit during interview sessions and providing document requests
·In coordination with the cluster PV Manager, EU-QPPV office and GPS, to investigate and provide/ support responses to inspection and audit findings, and implement Corrective and
Preventive actions
4. Agreements with third parties
·To collaborate with agreement owners, country QA and with the EMEA PV agreements team to ensure that any relevant Agreement with Third Party include appropriate PV clause or full SDEA
·To support the EMEA PV Agreement team in the implementation of local PSPs/MRPs, in collaboration with the initiator
·To notify safety signals to third party (distributor or PV supplier) in country/cluster as per procedure
·To perform reconciliation of Adverse Events with third party/PV Service Supplier
5. Other local PV activities
·To be involved in the communication on PV topics with national Competent Authorities, and supports answers preparation in cooperation with cluster PV Manager, GPS and Eu QPPV
·To perform surveillance activities for any new potential safety information (e.g. similar AEs reported in a cluster of reports or multiple cases for one batch received in a short time frame) and escalate as per procedures
·To alert the cluster PV Manager about any safety related issues without delay
·To prepare highlights as needed and represent PV at Nordic Quality Review Meeting (QMR)
·To be aware of required local risk minimization activities
·To perform local literature review, including assessment of local journals for screening, as described in SOP
·According to the process established at EU level, to validate the comparative table prepared by RA to put CCDS/CCSI/RSI and the local SPC in conformity
6. Regulatory intelligence
·Local regulatory intelligence: To regularly screen the websites of Competent Authorities in The Nordic countries for safety signals, Pharmacovigilance newsletters, regulations, etc
·To inform Pharmacovigilance Manager, EU QPPV and GPS on relevant changes concerning National regulations
7. Training:
·To perform trainings as required and keep up to date personal training records.
·To provide appropriate training on PV to new employees, partners and vendors
·To keep up to date records of the internal Pharmacovigilance trainings made to Baxter employees, partners or vendors
·To assist in onboarding and training of new team members
8. Procedures:
·To create, issue, implement and update local Pharmacovigilance related procedures as needed, in collaboration with the cluster PV team and Manager.
·To implement global Pharmacovigilance SOPs.
9. Compliance:
·To closely monitor local compliance and ensure all efforts are made to achieve high compliance rates.
·To open process errors according to SOPs and help in the resolution of noncompliance Reports
10. Activities related to associated countries in the Cluster:
·To collaborate closely with the UK Team members on above activities and provide any relevant information or support according to the cluster model

Why Join K.D. Feddersen Recycling Solutions?
K.D. Feddersen Recycling Solutions is looking for a Business Director who wants to lead, develop and shape a business area experiencing strong market demand. The company is part of the Feddersen Group, with operations worldwide and a particularly strong presence across Europe and the Baltic region.

As Business Director – Recycling, you will hold full budget and P&L responsibility for the business area. You will lead and support employees across the Nordic region while remaining actively involved in customer relationships, key account management and business development.

Strong negotiation skills and confidence in customer-facing situations.

Fluent in both Swedish and English.

Preferred Experience

Knowledge of the plastics, recycling or process industries.

Takes initiative, drives results and thrives in a dynamic environment.

Is humble, approachable and enjoys staying close to both customers and colleagues.

We are looking for an ambitious, commercially minded Finance Lead to join a fast-scaling AI company backed by NVIDIA, Microsoft, and AWS, and to grow with it.
About Antrino
Antrino Labs is building the platform that makes every square meter intelligent.
The physical world runs on processes nobody can actually see. Goods move, machines idle, space goes unused, and decisions about all of it are based on samples, guesses, and reports written after the fact. Antrino lets any organization deploy vision intelligence into a physical space and get back what is actually happening there, as structured, real-time information it can act on.
We have grown from 6 people to a team of 28 in less than a year, closed our Seed round, announced together with Dagens Industri, and are registered with Inspektionen för strategiska produkter (ISP). Everything we build follows Privacy by Design.
The role
This is not a traditional accounting position. Half the job is making the financial foundation work exceptionally well: payroll, bookkeeping, tax, payments, reporting, and administration, together with our founders and external advisers. The other half is commercial: working with the founders on pricing, business models, cost structures, and where the company puts its money.
One day you might be running payroll and closing the month. The next, you could be modeling the economics of deploying our platform across hundreds of customer sites, finding a European innovation grant, or helping the CEO evaluate a new commercial opportunity.
What you will work on
• Bookkeeping, reconciliations, and monthly and annual closing in Fortnox.
• Payroll, benefits, reimbursements, VAT, and tax, together with our auditors and banks.
• Invoicing, supplier payments, accounts payable and receivable, and corporate cards (Mynt).
• Filings with Bolagsverket and Skatteverket, board materials, minutes, and shareholder documentation.
• Budgets, forecasts, cash flow and runway models, and reporting for leadership, the board, and investors.
• Unit economics across cloud, AI inference, hardware, and deployment, and the margins they produce.
• Grants and non-dilutive funding from Swedish and European programmes.
• Replacing repetitive finance work with AI and modern software, so the function scales without its overhead growing at the same rate.
Who we are looking for
You are early in your career, with a strong financial foundation and an appetite for far more responsibility than you have today. You might be at a Big Four or mid-sized audit firm, an accounting agency, or in finance operations at a growing company.
• Around 2–4 years in accounting, auditing, or financial operations.
• Solid command of Swedish bookkeeping, payroll, and compliance, and hands-on experience with Fortnox or similar.
• Strong analytical skills and a real interest in modeling and commercial analysis.
• Excellent Swedish and English, written and spoken.
You take responsibility for the outcome, not just the task. You know payroll and tax have to be right every time while almost everything else moves fast, and you can hold both. You do not wait to be asked before fixing a process or chasing an opportunity.
It is a plus if you have worked with startups or venture-backed companies, understand SaaS metrics and unit economics, or have applied for funding through Vinnova, Almi, or EU programmes. You do not need all of this. We care more about judgment and how fast you learn than about years on your CV.
Life at Antrino
You will join a team of driven, ambitious people who thrive at a fast pace and enjoy working together. We go to AI events, host our own, and end plenty of weeks with an afterwork. Things change quickly here, and everyone's work is visible in what the company becomes.
What we offer
• Direct work with the CEO and board members on financial and commercial decisions.
• Exposure to fundraising, investor relations, and international expansion.
• Potential participation in our stock option programme after the probationary period.
• Freedom to improve systems, challenge processes, and bring AI into finance work.
• AI events, afterworks, team activities, and travel when the business requires it.
• Occupational pension, insurance, and friskvårdsbidrag.
Process
1. Introductory conversation about your background and ambitions.
2. Finance and accounting conversation about your hands-on experience.
3. Practical working session on a realistic scenario in operations, forecasting, or a commercial decision. We care how you think.
4. Conversation with the founders about options and terms.
We review applications continuously. References may be requested at the final stage.
Apply with your CV and a short note on why you want to move beyond traditional accounting into helping build a technology company.

Job Scope 
High level purpose of function. 

A Senior Vision Automation Engineer in a cell manufacturing company plays a key role in developing, optimizing, reverse-engineering, and maintaining machine vision and optical inspection systems to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations. They are responsible for programming, troubleshooting, and improving cameras, lighting configurations, and image processing algorithms, supporting both legacy production line re-commissioning and new vision system installations. The role also includes ensuring accurate data transfer, system connectivity, and smooth communication with PLCs, SCADA, and upper-level MES platforms to enable inline defect traceability, dimensional inspection, and digital integration. Close collaboration with production, engineering, and maintenance teams is required to identify and implement solutions that improve quality, throughput, and equipment uptime. A strong focus is placed on continuous improvement, safety, and scalability to meet the growing demand for electric vehicle battery production. 

Key Responsibilities 
Overall areas of responsibilities and activities 

Participate in HAZOP sessions and ensure compliance with process safety, operational safety, and environmental standards relating to equipment control and programming.  

Responsible for the FATs of the equipment (Project timeline dependent).  

Lead vision system integration and optical calibration during equipment commissioning and line re-starts (Project timeline dependent). 

Develop and reverse-engineer the vision inspection systems to be implemented in the production and logistics equipment in the factory, as well as the relevant specifications and documentation. 

Author and review engineering design documentation (Specifications, Functional design, Logic diagrams, Test Cases, Test Records).  

Train and mentor new engineers, and educate other support functions on machine vision, optics, and quality inspection gates. 

Code review and test of suppliers' vision software and algorithmic work within the projects to validate specified defect detection thresholds (Gauge R&R) and to ensure the quality and reliability of the data transferred from the equipment to the upper-level systems. 

Participate in R&D activities for piloting of new technologies and their suitability to production environments. 

Define and improve the factory blueprint, general specifications and ways of working in collaboration with the extended automation and digitalization teams. (Project timeline dependent). 

Contribute to technical improvements, development and optimization of software processes internally in the automation team 

The role requires regular presence on the production floor, with a minimum of approximately 25% of working hours spent on-site. Depending on project needs (such as line re-commissioning), there may be periods where up to 100% of working hours are required on the shop floor. 
Develop and maintain machine vision and image processing programming standards. 

Guide and mentor colleagues to industrial best practices, focussing on growth and development. 

Complete supplementary tasks as seen fit by management to effectively utilize time and resource for the benefit of the business. 

Requirements 
Educational background and previous experience required for the role 

Qualifications and Experience 

Masters Degree in Electronics, Mechatronics, Electrical, Automation, Robotics, Software Engineering or similar. 

Minimum of 7 years of relevant work experience within Industrial Automation in process-driven or discrete manufacturing industries such as: Battery Cell, Automotive, Chemical, Paper, Semiconductors, Pharma, Food, Warehouses, etc. 

Experience of working with industrial camera systems, optical components, and lighting techniques, including the selection, configuration, and calibration of camera hardware for manufacturing inspection and process control applications 

Experience in the design, configuration, and deployment of machine vision systems including cameras, lighting, and vision software platforms such as Cognex, Halcon, or equivalent, with experience integrating vision outputs into PLC, SCADA, and MES environments via OPC connectivity. 

Experience developing and optimising image processing pipelines and vision algorithms for applications such as defect detection, pattern recognition, and dimensional verification, with familiarity with industrial communication protocols for vision system integration. 

Experience in writing technical documentation including inspection requirement specifications, algorithm validation reports, vision system configuration records, functional design, UML, test cases, and test records. 

Experience with image processing software and programming tools relevant to industrial vision applications, such as Python, C++, OpenCV, or equivalent vision libraries, with the ability to develop, test, and optimise vision algorithms for real-time manufacturing environments 

Experienced continuous improvement and root cause analysis. 

Specific skills 
Strong knowledge of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems. 

Knowledge of cybersecurity best practices for manufacturing systems. 

Highly autonomous with a proactive mindset and work ethic.  

Troubleshooting skills with diagnostic equipment. 

Ability to document technical problems concisely. 

Experience in coaching, upskilling, and mentoring engineers or technicians, with a demonstrable commitment to developing the technical capability of others within a production environment. 

Excellent English skills, both written and oral, are essential. Basic Swedish and other language skills are a plus. You should have good communication skills and be able to work in close collaboration with colleagues from many different teams. 

Ability to work within varying environments including clean-rooms and dry-rooms, while wearing appropriate PPE. 

Comfortable operating in high-profile, international, and high-pressure environments. 

A genuine technical interest and passion about working within production is highly valued.

As part of building our Maintenance Engineering organization, we are expanding our team with a Process Equipment Engineer focused on our Furnace Area. The team and the area
You will be part of the Maintenance Engineering organization and report to the Maintenance Manager. The Teams purpose is to provide technical leadership for assigned equipment and work closely with Team Managers, Service Technicians, Maintenance Engineers, Process Engineers, Area Managers, and external suppliers.
The Furnace Area is an important part of our production and includes advanced high-temperature processes such as epitaxy, Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD), and thermal oxidation. These processes are used to grow and deposit controlled material layers and to form high-quality oxide films, making stable temperature profiles, gas flows, pressure, and equipment conditions essential to product quality and process repeatability. You will bridge equipment maintenance and process engineering, using equipment data, process results, and production feedback to identify causes of instability, improve uptime and utilization, and ensure that technical actions are coordinated across teams.
About the role
As a Process Equipment Engineer, you will be responsible for the technical health, reliability, and continuous improvement of equipment within the Furnace Area. Equipment is your primary discipline, supported by process knowledge that enables effective fault analysis, improvement work, and close collaboration with Process Engineers.
You will act as the technical lead for the assigned equipment, guide service technicians, coordinate technical escalations, and lead root cause analyses of downtime events and recurring failures. You will also develop equipment monitoring and preventive maintenance, define relevant KPIs, contribute to equipment purchases and upgrades, and serve as a technical contact for suppliers.
In this role, you will:

Act as the technical lead for assigned furnace equipment, guiding service technicians and leading complex troubleshooting, root cause analyses, and follow-up of corrective actions.

Manage technical escalation plans and coordinate equipment status, priorities, and actions with Team Managers, Process Engineers, and suppliers.

Use equipment and process data to identify causes of instability, define and follow up KPIs such as uptime, MTBF, and MTTR, and improve equipment monitoring through equipment dashboard and SPC.

Develop preventive maintenance routines, maintain technical documentation, and contribute to equipment purchases, installations, upgrades, and spare-part planning.

Lead equipment-related risk analyses and ensure LOTO and other safety requirements are reflected in maintenance routines, documentation, and training.

We are looking for someone who has:

A Master’s degree in a relevant field, such as Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Electronics, or a related discipline.

At least five years of relevant experience in manufacturing with strong equipment-related knowledge and an understanding of production processes. Experience in semiconductor or MEMS process development or manufacturing is an advantage.

Experience with root cause analysis, data analysis, SPC, quality-control methods, equipment monitoring, and preventive maintenance systems.

Proficiency in English, particularly in technical terminology and documentation. Swedish is considered as highly meritorious.

To thrive in this role, you enjoy working analytically and finding practical solutions to complex technical challenges. You take a structured and proactive approach to your work, communicate clearly with different stakeholders, and are comfortable guiding others. With several activities often running in parallel, you are also able to prioritize effectively and ensure that actions are documented and followed through.
What we offer you

The opportunity to work with cutting-edge MEMS technology and some of the most advanced equipment in the industry.

A technically challenging environment where you solve complex problems and continuously develop your expertise.

A varied role in which new challenges, technologies, and improvement opportunities make every day different.

About Silex
Silex is the world’s largest and most advanced pure-play MEMS foundry, headquartered in Stockholm. MEMS is present in nearly all modern technology, from personal gadgets to automotive electronics, medical monitoring and testing equipment, and thermal management systems. With a team of expert engineers, operators, technicians, support staff, specialists, and more, Silex brings the ideas and concepts of the industry’s leading MEMS innovators to life.
The recruitment process
We have an ongoing recruitment process and therefore encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. To apply, please attach your CV and answer a few questions. Our process is competency-based and includes a personality and logic test as well as reference checks. Additionally, we will conduct a background check and drug test prior to employment, and as an employer, we perform random alcohol and drug tests for all employees.

YOU WILL

About Taigatech
We solve some of the most important problems in industry with AI and computer vision. With our connection to the latest research and academia, we take world-leading research in AI and computer vision and turn it into impactful solutions that help the wood industry increase yield, availability, and productivity.
Technology is reshaping our world. We believe the forest and wood products have an important role to play in a sustainable future, and AI is how the industry gets there.
We are a growing team in a comfortable office in central Gothenburg, working closely with many of the leading names in wood processing. Our systems run in production at sawmills and pulp mills in Sweden and abroad. There's no better time to join our journey than now.
Why this role exists
Our systems create value the moment their output reaches the customer's control system — a correction, a signal, something the line can act on.
What determines the results are a handful of decisions made early and made well: which signal, where it lands, what the line does with it, and how it behaves when something unexpected happens. Get those right and the implementation is small and quick.
Today that judgement is distributed between our own team and the automation partners we work with on each installation. We want someone to decide what the interface should look like, judge whether it came out right, decide when a sensor or other component needs replacing, and if the signal belongs on a different fieldbus.
That's the person we're hiring. You don't replace our automation partners. You become the one who leads them.
What you'll do
The role is both technical and leadership, and the balance shifts from project to project.
Own the machine-side interface. You decide how our system talks to the customer's PLC. Signals, timing, handshakes, watchdog, fail-safe behaviour. You write the functional description the work is built from.
Lead our automation partners. Sometimes that means writing the code snippet yourself. Sometimes it means explaining what needs doing and reviewing that it came out right. You decide which.
Make the technical decisions on the customer's plant. Upgrading a component for better results, or moving to a different fieldbus, is yours to propose and drive. The implementation itself normally goes to a partner.
Be the customer's main contact through the project — scope, timeline, status, time and cost reporting. You take over from sales and carry the delivery home.
Clear the path. OT network access, change control, and the dialogue with the site's automation and IT departments, so the installation can be done quickly and safely.
Work closely with our ML and vision engineers. Translate what the process needs into what the model has to output, and the model's limits back into what we can promise.
Make it repeatable. A reusable interface specification, a commissioning checklist, and a growing network of automation partners to deliver alongside.
Who you are
You need experience, but we don't care how many years you have behind you. We care about what you've done.
You have programmed PLCs in live production, on at least one major platform — Siemens TIA/S7, Beckhoff, ABB, Mitsubishi, Codesys or equivalent
You have hands-on experience of industrial networks: Profinet, Profibus, EtherCAT, Modbus TCP, OPC UA or equivalent.
You have extended control systems you did not write with retrofits onto existing, running equipment
You have written functional descriptions that someone else built from
You have stood on site during commissioning, with production running and someone waiting
Drives the project forward by keeping people accountable, asking the right questions, and pushing decisions when it matters — even when that means a difficult conversation.
Swedish and English, and you sometimes travel to sites
Bonus
Sawmill, pulp and paper, or other heavy process industry
Vision systems, sensors or measurement equipment
Experience on the supplier side, responsible for subcontractors
Machinery directive and risk assessment on modified lines
Python and basic data analysis
What we offer
You'll be our first dedicated automation hire. You set the delivery process, and it becomes the standard we scale on. As delivery volume grows, the function gets built around you.
You'll work directly with the founders, with our ML engineers and with the mills themselves. Office in Gothenburg.
We review applications on a rolling basis.
Öppen för alla
Vi fokuserar på din kompetens, inte dina övriga förutsättningar. Vi är öppna för att anpassa rollen eller arbetsplatsen efter dina behov.
